verdict.rationale: The Ryzen AI software stack for this chip offers non-GUI, scriptable entry points: a command-line NPU management utility (xrt-smi), Python/C++ ONNX Runtime APIs, and a server interface that apps in any language can call, on supported Linux distributions. Together these imply the chip can be driven headlessly, but nothing documents headless or CI operation directly. Missing for 10: explicit headless/CI documentation, CI runner or container guidance, and hands-on reports of automated pipeline use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The xrt-smi utility is a command-line interface to monitor and manage the NPU integrated AMD CPUs.
This allows applications written in any language (C#, JavaScript, Python, C++, etc.) to easily integrate with Ryzen AI LLMs.
The AI model is deployed using the ONNX Runtime with either C++ or Python APIs.
Windows 11 - 64-Bit Edition , RHEL x86 64-Bit , Ubuntu x86 64-Bit
